opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Edward Fleming (E042) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access, and admin only if their role owns the system (Source Code is owned by Engineer). Recommended level: write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E042: contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Requested write, but max for this employee is read. Recommended level: read.
reason: There is conflicting information about Edward Fleming (E042). HR records indicate full-time Payroll Specialist (max write for Source Code), but Security records indicate contractor with basic security training (max read for Source Code, since write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting employment-type facts and that access policy must not be exceeded, I apply the more restrictive maximum. Read is at or below the requested write level and does not violate the contractor limitation.
